title: Critical Field / 16-track performable album research
classification: 16 complete written composition specifications. NOT 16 rendered musical files. Current repository studies/010 already contains 8 prototype renders reported locally, pending human listening.
goal: Eight mechanisms, two materially different 3–5-minute compositions each, 4 minutes nominal, actual local render and review required.
constrained_stack: Existing installed Waveform 14.1.24 (Free entitlement and save/reopen/export still unverified), Surge XT 1.3.4, plugdata 0.9.3; optional available licensed Ableton and SuperCollider for custom DSP. Do not purchase plugins.
studio_status: Research briefs committed; no local render/AVP/venue tests conducted by this commit.

families.name: MICRO / DATA PRECISION
families.lineage: Ryoji Ikeda: +/- (1996), matrix (2000), dataplex (2005), test pattern (2008). Learn perceptual scale and extreme precision, not his exact frequencies or imagery.
families.mechanism: A sparse quantized event lattice, stable micro-events, one rare disruptive event. The grid must make musical sense without white flashing.
families.instrument: Bitfield Instrument: scheduled impulses + resonant filter bank + sub-pulse; quantization, probability and negative-space gates. A Surge XT metallic pluck is a sketch fallback; plugdata/SC can provide original event DSP.

tracks.title: Unit Cell
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:38 establish three timbral classes; 0:38–1:22 one clock with holes; 1:22–2:10 exact sub events create body; 2:10–3:02 remove most events, preserve a 5-step motif; 3:02–4:00 accelerated return then near-silence.
tracks.differentiation: Event geometry is slow enough that each click has a function; dynamics from interval and silence, not loudness.
tracks.mix_fx: No full-bus reverb; only two bright hits to 0.15–0.4s early reflections; short tempo-free delay on isolated events.
tracks.controls: precision → scheduling grid tightness; aperture → exposed voices; PINCH triggers rare structure reversal.
tracks.visual: single grid cell → an ordered field; same event IDs trigger light points.

tracks.title: Error Horizon
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:27 static precise click; 0:27–1:08 deliberate nonperiodic omissions; 1:08–1:53 micro-events accelerate while pitch register moves down; 1:53–2:38 hard silence + low-only events; 2:38–3:30 bounded overload; 3:30–4:00 break down to one original pulse.
tracks.differentiation: An intentionally broken syntax and negative space, NOT the previous track at a faster BPM.
tracks.mix_fx: Spectral narrowing versus widening is the primary effect. Keep headroom and harsh high-frequency safety; no sustained high-level tones.
tracks.controls: fault → omission/insert rate; scale → micro-to-architectural grouping; FOOT toggles source/derived grid.
tracks.visual: error codes fracture and reorganize spatial geometry; avoid imitation of artist-specific data visualizations.

families.name: RHYTHMIC MACHINES
families.lineage: Byetone's Plastic Star / Death of a Typographer (2008), Symeta (2011), combined with user's original 26s Listening_02 observations. Develop original rhythmic identities.
families.mechanism: Elastic sub, percussion with identifiable transients, staggered call/response; silence is a groove device.
families.instrument: Rubber Drum/Metal Transient: FM pitch sweep, short resonator, velocity-dependent timbre and transient/body separation; Surge XT + plugdata custom hit shaper.

tracks.title: Recoil
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:31 percussive bass calls; 0:31–1:20 two complementary percussion replies; 1:20–1:55 remove kick and expose syncopation; 1:55–2:52 structural groove return with new answer; 2:52–3:35 phase-delayed metallic texture; 3:35–4:00 abrupt dry exit.
tracks.differentiation: Genuine call and response; one two-bar groove grows by replacing events, never by continuous clutter.
tracks.mix_fx: Short slap delay on metal only, hard dry transient front; sidechain/release tuned to bass notes and kick, no huge reverb.
tracks.controls: bounce → pitch-envelope elastic tension; dialogue → call/answer balance; FOOT launches a deliberate breakdown.
tracks.visual: impact geometry; original bass attacks are same events as short-lived volumetric deformations.

tracks.title: Shear Force
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:47 sub-only tension; 0:47–1:28 4+3 step asymmetry; 1:28–2:12 fractured kick and one exposed midrange signature; 2:12–2:53 complete rhythmic subtraction; 2:53–3:33 one decisive transformation and deep impact; 3:33–4:00 heavy, slow deceleration.
tracks.differentiation: Architectural rupture, nonstandard phrase grouping, and earned contrast; not a louder Recoil.
tracks.mix_fx: Parallel distorted midrange bus with dry sub preserved, short metallic space, 1–2 event-locked long tails.
tracks.controls: shear → clock disagreement; impact → bounded bass/timbre pressure; FOOT triggers rupture.
tracks.visual: a rigid structure shears and reforms on the same override event.

families.name: SPATIAL / SPECTRAL ARCHITECTURE
families.lineage: Ryoichi Kurokawa early Copynature/READ to rheo; scene is conceived as sound+image from the outset. Not a copy of his datasets or shots.
families.mechanism: One multidimensional spatial field with source location and timbral space sharing underlying coordinate/state.
families.instrument: Spectral Mesh: controlled bank of resonators fed by own field recordings + moving grains; plugdata biquad bank or SC Klank-like approach; optional real 4ch bus after rider verification.

tracks.title: Volumetric Weather
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:56 one captured environmental grain; 0:56–1:42 timbral altitude shift; 1:42–2:18 wide stillness; 2:18–3:11 weather front/pitched resonance moves through field; 3:11–4:00 evaporate to source recording.
tracks.differentiation: Mostly texture with genuinely evolving spectral form; no need for busy click track.
tracks.mix_fx: Three depth planes: near dry, medium early reflection, far late reverb; automate decay only during designed spatial transitions.
tracks.controls: altitude → resonant center; weather → cloud density; position → speaker/stereo panning; manual gesture hold.
tracks.visual: a spatial volume with a legible near/far relationship. Stereo fallback uses meaningful depth, not fake verified surround.

tracks.title: Tectonic Glass
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:25 weak brittle contact; 0:25–1:14 resonance stabilizes into 3-note harmonic cell; 1:14–2:04 deformation causes partial frequency splits; 2:04–2:42 stop all high content; 2:42–3:24 one collapse / reconstitution; 3:24–4:00 small fragments fall away.
tracks.differentiation: Granular/spectral transformations form a time sculpture; structural impact without generic cinematic riser.
tracks.mix_fx: Multiband control for brittle highs; frequency-dependent room tails and pre-delay to preserve attacks.
tracks.controls: fracture → count of resonant shards; mass → low/medium harmonic weighting; PINCH capture.
tracks.visual: same fractured resonator graph also determines point-cloud connectivity.

families.name: COPY / RESYNTHESIS / MEMORY
families.lineage: Alva Noto's early Transform (2001) and Xerrox Vol.1 (2007): digital copying/misreading can be compositional material. Use only original input.
families.mechanism: Original source repeatedly transformed into structurally meaningful descendants, with a reversible lineage of sonic identity.
families.instrument: Copy Engine: local audio buffer, lossy/bit-depth variants, granular offset, spectral freeze, bounded feedback, preset snapshots; commit derived versions to disk for repeatability.

tracks.title: First Copy
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:50 expose one original contact/room sound; 0:50–1:42 one degree of degradation; 1:42–2:21 derived pitch becomes a counterline; 2:21–3:09 material turns spatial and distant; 3:09–4:00 near-perfect return with one missing detail.
tracks.differentiation: Source remains audible until the final transformation; it is a piece about remembering sound.
tracks.mix_fx: Convolution or early reflections tied to source, not constant wet pad. Two tempo-free echo distances separated by register.
tracks.controls: copy_depth → destructive lineage stage; memory → how many prior generations can answer; BUTTON commits a generation.
tracks.visual: source shape duplicates and misregisters; track generation IDs in shared score.

tracks.title: Xerographic Fault
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:40 original loop becomes a machine; 0:40–1:18 controlled copy errors form groove; 1:18–2:06 fast switching between generations; 2:06–2:36 rupture/dropped frame silence; 2:36–3:27 hard reassembled drum machine; 3:27–4:00 source unexpectedly returns clean.
tracks.differentiation: Rhythmic corruption rather than dreamy copying, with a genuinely new composition from intermediate generations.
tracks.mix_fx: Sample-rate reduction at selected transitions, transient-preserving delay for 2/4 events, low wet on sustained sources.
tracks.controls: corrupt → bit/segment transform index; repeat → re-insertion probability; FOOT restore original.
tracks.visual: temporal discontinuity is audible and visible with same generation markers.

families.name: FOUND-SOUND / CORPUS INSTRUMENT
families.lineage: Amon Tobin early Bricolage (1997), Permutation (1998), Supermodified (2000), Foley Room (2007), ISAM (2011): source transformation from recordings to playable instruments. Record your own sources.
families.mechanism: A small personal corpus of physically interesting original audio, segmented and played as an expressive instrument, not a sample pack montage.
families.instrument: Object Corpus: 20 self-recorded object/material hits; segmentation/transient detection; descriptors or manual metadata; mapping pitch, attack/decay, resonance and articulation. Optional FluCoMa if available and licensed.

tracks.title: Contact Archive
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:35 three original material contacts; 0:35–1:17 learn their articulation; 1:17–2:12 assign them a rhythmic dialogue; 2:12–2:54 stretch one into a quasi-melodic sustain; 2:54–3:28 return hits against the sustain; 3:28–4:00 end on an unprocessed object sound.
tracks.differentiation: Composed identity and original sound provenance, no generic drum rack substitutions.
tracks.mix_fx: Dry percussive foreground, one predelay/short resonant chamber on selected contacts, spatial motion meaningful to materials.
tracks.controls: material → corpus cluster; articulation → strike/scrape/resonate; PINCH commits a phrase.
tracks.visual: materials represented as simple spatial traces, not literal photos.

tracks.title: Object Swarm
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:25 isolate one mechanical contact; 0:25–1:06 derive a kick/bass from contact; 1:06–1:54 accelerating hocket of different materials; 1:54–2:22 tempo persists through sudden empty field; 2:22–3:20 multi-object groove fractures and resolves; 3:20–4:00 source solo becomes percussion again.
tracks.differentiation: One corpus as tightly produced dance/industrial system; not simply more of Contact Archive.
tracks.mix_fx: Per-material parallel distortion and envelope shaping; sub kept centered, bright shards with short spatial return.
tracks.controls: swarm → voice count with max polyphony; material_bias → selection distribution; FOOT mutes all but main pulse.
tracks.visual: number of spatial bodies corresponds to playing object-voices, event-synchronized.

families.name: PIANO / ELECTRONIC LONG FORM
families.lineage: KASHIWA Daisuke's piano/electronics and programmatic long-form, contrasted with user's current Afterimage. Extract musical processes, not notes or arrangements.
families.mechanism: A genuinely written ORIGINAL piano motif with directed harmonic, registral and rhythmic development; electronics changes the meaning of the motif.
families.instrument: Afterimage Piano: original MIDI + recorded/synthesized piano, delayed-event memory; resonator and granular counterpart; optional string-like harmonic layer.

tracks.title: Gravity Phrase
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:55 strong 2-bar phrase alone with expressive dynamics; 0:55–1:34 counterline changes cadence; 1:34–2:23 low spectral shadow answers harmony; 2:23–3:06 remove most notes, slow harmonic transformation; 3:06–4:00 original motif returns in changed register/chord then stops.
tracks.differentiation: Narrative driven by original harmonic tension and real phrasing, not repeating high notes with stock strings.
tracks.mix_fx: Dry piano anchors center; spectral resonance creates one 'shadow' role; short and long space buses contrasted at returns.
tracks.controls: memory → delayed phrase history; harmonic_weight → note/chord voicing density; foot cue instead of arbitrary note control.
tracks.visual: motif traces appear later as delayed paths; scene changes on true harmonic arrivals.

tracks.title: Luminous Afterimage
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:39 incomplete motif; 0:39–1:20 clear answered phrase; 1:20–2:02 rhythm enters with carefully staggered counterline; 2:02–2:45 remove bass and make harmony weightless; 2:45–3:29 delayed phrase returns in altered harmony; 3:29–4:00 final release with the original melodic material and limited tail.
tracks.differentiation: A brighter narrative outcome, with distinct chords, gesture of arrival and remembered theme; not merely Gravity Phrase transposed.
tracks.mix_fx: Avoid global hall reverb; keep intimate leading attacks and create tails only on phrase endings. Stereo image should move slowly.
tracks.controls: phrase_release → orchestrated scene change; color → harmonic/filtered counterpart; optional small gestural rubato bounded by tempo clock.
tracks.visual: from restricted lattice to spacious field; calm release after the stage peak.

families.name: EMBODIED / INTERACTION-COMPOSED
families.lineage: Daito Manabe's 2008 myoelectric/face instrument research plus later algorithmic and agent systems. Vision Pro DJ public video is evidence of a demonstration, not open technical implementation.
families.mechanism: The performer changes a musical system's rules, not 50 raw synth knobs. Work first with desktop/MIDI replay before real AVP and never imply actual EMG capture.
families.instrument: Gesture Voltage: dual state engines; stable glide, event hysteresis, hand zone control; self-contained OSC MIDI fallback; spectral/timbral pressure is bounded and neutral-safe.

tracks.title: Virtual Muscle
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:33 dry repeated motor phrase; 0:33–1:16 a virtual effort envelope changes harmonic excitation; 1:16–2:08 voice modulations interact; 2:08–2:50 controlled failure / loss of tracking changes nothing unsafe; 2:50–3:30 recover with new melodic contour; 3:30–4:00 fade effort, leave source.
tracks.differentiation: Movement articulation and instrument response are compositional; gesture dynamics are recorded/replayable, not random automation.
tracks.mix_fx: Bounded pressure→saturation with dry bypass, transient-safe multiband envelope, stereo movement never on master gain.
tracks.controls: effort (simulated/derived) → pressure; pinch edge→event; dwell→hold; FOOT→recover/kill.
tracks.visual: show both human control and system state, using hand skeleton only if actual tracking is available.

tracks.title: Override Gesture
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:41 one audible decision changes rhythm; 0:41–1:32 player locks an unstable beat; 1:32–2:14 tension grows with declining event density; 2:14–2:40 deliberate long near-silence; 2:40–3:25 one foot override creates decisive sonic/spatial change; 3:25–4:00 performer chooses deconstruction.
tracks.differentiation: Single performable moment, strong agency and peak contrast; not just more modulated sounds.
tracks.mix_fx: High-impact short transient plus long, carefully bounded spectral tail; dry sub and transient peak checked; manual hard mute independent of network.
tracks.controls: FOOT OVERRIDE is priority; left/right gestures shape pre/post-event state. tracking stale→neutral.
tracks.visual: same event.id deforms both speaker-scene and large spatial geometry; flash rules controlled for audience safety.

families.name: TIME / ORBITAL SEQUENCER
families.lineage: Original Stage Casting 04 time-space instrument line; technical relation to Max, MIDI and spatial performance rather than copying artist-specific work.
families.mechanism: Multiple voiced clocks and spatial paths that can re-align; a sequencer that produces meaningful notes, rests and phrases.
families.instrument: Orbital Hocket: three bounded phase oscillators, Euclidean-ish gates, MIDI note selector, quantized transition, OSC phase/state publisher. Tempo remains in one authoritative clock.

tracks.title: Orbital Hocket
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:34 one clock and one tone; 0:34–1:19 two voices exchange notes rather than overlap; 1:19–2:05 third clock adds long-range cycle; 2:05–2:46 clocks briefly coincide; 2:46–3:31 voice order inverts into a more physical groove; 3:31–4:00 unravel to initial clock.
tracks.differentiation: Hocket and voice role exchange, not randomized 16th sequence flood.
tracks.mix_fx: Tempo-related ping delays on two voice outputs, no global wet wash; clear front-to-back separation.
tracks.controls: phase → musical time divergence; orbit → spatialization; BUTTON quantizes realignment at bar boundary.
tracks.visual: three orbital paths share exact clock state and note event IDs.

tracks.title: Phase Zero
tracks.arrangement: 0:00–0:21 nearly empty synchrony; 0:21–1:03 progressively displaced accent layers; 1:03–1:52 long composite rhythm emerges; 1:52–2:26 remove strong grid to reveal hidden periodicity; 2:26–3:23 one successful realignment becomes the climax; 3:23–4:00 clocks reset at different speeds to silence.
tracks.differentiation: The peak is a structural realignment and a new rhythm, not just increased BPM or notes.
tracks.mix_fx: Very dry attacks and explicitly selected stereo echo points; short reverb only in the late afterpulse.
tracks.controls: divergence → phase ratio bound; density → max event voices; FOOT realign; SAFE reset authoritative clock.
tracks.visual: spatial orbit coincidence coincides with sonic phase alignment, not unrelated FFT reactivity.
